I told the representative that I could not make the first payment until XX/XX/XXXX. I was told by the customer service representative that there would be no late charges and no interest as long as I made my payments each month. I received a letter dated XX/XX/XXXX confirming the agreement. 

I made the monthly payments beginning XX/XX/XXXX as agreed. I continued to make payments each month for the agreed amount. On XX/XX/XXXX I received a letter dated XX/XX/XXXX stating that I had missed XXXX or more payments. I contacted Citibank on XX/XX/XXXX to dispute the letter. I made four phone calls trying to resolve the matter. I was told by each representative that they showed no notes of a payment arrangement even though I referred to the letter confirming the arrangement and pointed out that all interest charges had ceased as agreed. 

I attempted to make a payment on XX/XX/XXXX to honor the agreement but was unable to make a payment. I contacted Citi Cards on XX/XX/XXXX and spoke with a representative to no avail. I requested a supervisor to resolve the issues. I was told by the representative that unless I explained why I need to speak with a supervisor she would not be able to transfer my call. I also attempted to speak with a supervisor on the previous call and was placed on hold for more than an hour. I was told that the account had been charged off on XX/XX/XXXX and reported to the credit reporting agencies. 

I did not default on the payment arrangement and now there is a charge off on my credit report and also Citi Card continued to report my account as being more than 30 days delinquent despite the payment agreement.

Subject : Complaint Regarding Violation of TILA, Breach of Contract, and Unresolved Recoupment Request for Account # ending XXXX with Capital One Auto Finance Co. 

Consumer Information : Full Name : Provided Upon Request Account Number : ending XXXX Summary of the Issue : I am filing this complaint due to Capital One Auto Finance Co.s violation of the Truth in Lending Act ( TILA ) 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq., breach of contract, failure to provide a complete audit of my account, and refusal to comply with my lawful requests for recoupment. Capital Ones actions have resulted in financial harm and the misclassification of my account, in violation of federal statutes and consumer rights. 

Background : On XX/XX/XXXX, I entered into a contractual agreement with Capital One Auto Finance Co. through its broker, XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX, involving the purchase of a XXXX XXXX XXXX. The agreement included a promissory note that was later transferred without recourse and securitized. I have since discovered that the transfer and sale of this note were not fully disclosed, contravening TILAs mandate for transparency and failing to inform me of the true nature of my financial obligations. 

Despite multiple attempts to resolve this matter, including a formal Opportunity to Cure letter sent via registered mail, Capital One has refused to provide written responses and a complete audit of my account as required by 12 CFR Part 226 ( Regulation Z ) and the Fair Credit Billing Act ( FCBA ) 15 U.S.C. 1666. Capital Ones refusal to respond in writing directly conflicts with the contractual terms that allow for amendments in writing, thereby breaching our agreement.

Specific Violations : Violation of TILA ( 15 U.S.C. 1601 et seq. ) : Capital One failed to provide full disclosure of the transfer, sale, and securitization of my promissory note, depriving me of my right to informed consent.

Breach of Contract : Capital Ones refusal to provide a written audit and its failure to recognize my right to settle the account through written amendments constitute a breach of our contractual terms and their fiduciary duty.

Failure to Act in Good Faith ( UCC 1-304 ) : Capital Ones handling of my promissory note and refusal to provide transparency violate the standards of good faith in financial transactions.

I immediately requested the bill from the city, which had to be mailed to me. On XX/XX/XXXX, after receiving the bill I faxed the notice and bill to the fax number provided and received a confirmation of receipt. I faxed that notification and bill to the same escrow account fax number at The Money Source, receiving a confirmation of receipt. At that point, I made a phone call to The Money Source and voiced my concerns and asked that someone immediately investigate. Two months later on XX/XX/XXXX, I received a notice that a lien had been placed on my home and it was to be sold on the courthouse steps on XX/XX/XXXX for failure to pay property taxes. DEVICE PROTECTION PLAN TERMS
Issued by Voltguard Protection Ltd
In this policy, "the Provider" means Voltguard Protection Ltd and "the Customer" means the person named in the schedule.

§ 1  Definitions
(1) Accessories means cases, chargers, earbuds and styluses.
(2) Accessories means cases, chargers and earbuds.
(3) Assessed loss means the cost of repair or replacement agreed by the Provider, before any service fee, limit or sublimit is applied.
(4) Authorised repairer means a repairer approved in writing by the Provider.
(5) Battery replacement means replacement batteries and battery repairs.
(6) Breakdown means the failure of a part to work as the manufacturer intended, from an internal electrical or mechanical fault.
(7) Business day means Monday to Friday, excluding public holidays.
(8) Device means the item shown in the schedule, bought new from an authorised retailer.
(9) Family means the Customer's spouse or partner and any children who live with the Customer.
(10) Incident means a single event, or a series of events arising from one cause.
(11) Limit means the most the Provider will pay for all claims under a section arising from one incident.
(12) Manufacturer's warranty period means the first 24 months after the device was bought.
(13) Policy period means twelve months from the policy start date shown in the Customer's schedule.
(14) Premium means the amount the Customer must pay for this policy, including any taxes.
(15) Proof of purchase means an original receipt, invoice or bank statement showing the item, the price and the date.
(16) Receipt means a document from the seller or provider showing the date, the amount paid and what was supplied.
(17) Replacement device means a device of the same or similar specification, which may be refurbished.
(18) Schedule means the document issued with this policy that shows the Customer's details, the covers the Customer bought and any extensions.
(19) Sublimit means a lower limit that applies to a particular class of property or treatment within a section.
(20) Wearables means smartwatches and fitness trackers.

§ 2  Limits and service fee
(1) Accidental Damage: limit $800 per incident; service fee $79 per claim.
(2) Breakdown: limit $600 per incident; service fee $25 per claim.
(3) Theft and Loss: limit $1,200 per incident; service fee $99 per claim.
(4) The service fee is deducted from the assessed loss before any limit or sublimit is applied.

§ 3  Severability
(1) If any term of this policy is found to be invalid, the remaining terms will continue in full force.

§ 4  Assignment
(1) The Customer cannot transfer the Customer's interest in this policy to anyone else without the Provider's written consent.

§ 5  Communication
(1) The Provider will communicate with the Customer in English.
(2) The Provider may record telephone calls for training and quality purposes.

§ 6  Optional cover: Theft and Loss
(1) The Provider will replace the Customer's device if it is stolen or lost.
(2) This section applies only if it is shown as purchased in the Customer's schedule.
(3) The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
(4) The Provider will not pay for loss or theft of property left unattended in a vehicle or in a public place. This exclusion does not apply to property locked out of sight in the boot or trunk of a locked vehicle.
(5) The Provider will not pay for theft that was not reported to the police.

§ 7  Subrogation
(1) The Provider will be entitled to take over and conduct in the Customer's name the defence or settlement of any claim.
(2) The Provider can take action in the Customer's name to recover any payment the Provider makes from anyone responsible for the loss.

§ 8  Change of address
(1) The Customer must tell the Provider within 30 days if the Customer changes the Customer's address.
(2) The Provider may change the premium or the terms from the date of the move.

§ 9  Arbitration
(1) If the Provider accepts a claim but disagree with the Customer about the amount, the difference will be referred to an arbitrator appointed by both parties.
(2) Where arbitration applies, obtaining an award is a condition precedent to any legal action against the Provider.

§ 10  Currency
(1) All amounts in this policy are in US dollars.
(2) Claims for costs incurred in another currency will be converted at the exchange rate on the date the cost was incurred.

§ 11  Breakdown
(1) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it stops working because of an electrical or mechanical fault.
(2) No cover applies under this section to any incident that happens within the first 45 days after the policy start date.
(3) The most the Provider will pay for Battery replacement under this section is $80 per incident.
(4) The Provider will not pay for breakdowns during the manufacturer's warranty period.
(5) The Provider will not pay for breakdown caused by liquid getting into the device.

§ 12  Joint policyholders
(1) Where more than one person is named in the schedule, each of them is treated as having knowledge of anything any of them knows.
(2) A notice sent to one named person is treated as sent to all of them.

§ 13  Notices
(1) Any notice the Provider gives under this policy will be sent to the most recent postal or email address the Provider holds.
(2) Notices from the Customer should be sent to the address shown in the schedule.

§ 14  Compensation scheme
(1) The Provider is covered by a financial services compensation scheme.
(2) If the Provider cannot meet the Provider's obligations, the Customer may be entitled to compensation from the scheme, depending on the type of policy and the circumstances.

§ 15  Changes in circumstances
(1) The Customer must tell the Provider as soon as reasonably possible about any change in the information shown in the schedule.
(2) The Provider may then change the premium or the terms of this policy, or cancel it.

§ 16  Discounts
(1) Any discount shown in the schedule applies only while the conditions for it continue to be met.
(2) If a condition for a discount stops being met, the Provider may charge the premium without the discount from that date.

§ 17  Software support
(1) The Provider's helpline can give advice on setting up and using the Customer's device.
(2) Software support does not include fixing problems caused by third-party apps or unofficial operating systems.

§ 18  Market conditions
(1) If the replacement item is no longer available, the Provider will pay the cost of the nearest equivalent available at the time of the claim.

§ 19  Renewal
(1) The Provider will write to the Customer at least 21 days before the end of the policy period with the renewal terms.
(2) The Provider is not obliged to offer renewal.

§ 20  Reasonable precautions
(1) The Customer must take all reasonable steps to prevent loss or damage and to keep property in good condition.
(2) The Customer must take reasonable steps to recover lost or stolen property.

§ 21  Recovery of costs
(1) If the Provider pays a claim that is later found not to be covered, the Provider may ask the Customer to repay the amount.

§ 22  Duty of fair presentation
(1) The Customer must answer all questions the Provider asks honestly and to the best of the Customer's knowledge.
(2) If the Customer gives incorrect information deliberately or recklessly, the Provider may treat this policy as if it never existed and keep the premium.
(3) If the Customer gives incorrect information carelessly, the Provider may reduce any claim payment in proportion to the premium that should have been charged.

§ 23  Salvage
(1) When the Provider replaces an item, the damaged or recovered item becomes the Provider's property.
(2) If stolen property is recovered after the Provider has paid a claim, the Customer must tell the Provider and either return the payment or give the Provider the property.

§ 24  Environmental commitment
(1) Where practical, the Provider will repair rather than replace damaged items and will use recycled or refurbished parts.
(2) The Customer may ask for a new part instead, and the Provider will tell the Customer whether any additional cost would apply.

§ 25  Cooperation
(1) The Customer must give the Provider all the help and information the Provider reasonably need to settle a claim.
(2) The Customer must not admit liability or offer to settle any claim without the Provider's written permission.

§ 26  Exchange of information
(1) To prevent fraud, the Provider may check the details the Customer gives against public records and industry databases.
(2) The Provider may contact previous insurers to confirm the Customer's claims history.

§ 27  Waiver
(1) If the Provider does not enforce any term of this policy, that does not mean the Provider has given up the right to enforce it later.

§ 28  Accessibility
(1) This document is available in large print, braille or audio on request.

§ 29  Accidental Damage
(1) The Provider will repair or replace the Customer's device if it is accidentally damaged.
(2) The most the Provider will pay for Accessories under this section is $100 per incident.
(3) The most the Provider will pay for Wearables under this section is $250 per incident.
(4) The Provider will not pay for cosmetic damage, such as scratches or dents, that does not affect how the device works.
(5) The Provider will not pay for damage following a repair by anyone other than the Provider or an authorised repairer. This exclusion does not apply if the Provider approved the repair in writing beforehand.

§ 30  Interest
(1) The Provider will not pay interest on any claim payment unless the law requires it.

§ 31  General exclusions
(1) The Provider will not pay for loss caused by nuclear radiation or radioactive contamination.
(2) The Provider will not pay for loss or damage caused by war, invasion, or civil war.
(3) The Provider will not pay for any fraudulent claim or any claim supported by false documents.
(4) The Provider will not pay for loss arising from a government order or sanction that prohibits the Provider from paying.

§ 32  Fraud
(1) If any claim is fraudulent or exaggerated in any respect, the Provider will not pay the claim and all cover under this policy may be cancelled.
(2) The Provider may share information with fraud prevention agencies and other insurers.

§ 33  Premium payment
(1) The Customer must pay the premium on or before the policy start date or in the monthly instalments shown in the schedule.
(2) If an instalment is not paid within 14 days of its due date, the Provider may cancel the policy after giving notice.

§ 34  Third-party administrators
(1) The Provider may appoint another company to handle claims or other services on the Provider's behalf.
(2) Any company the Provider appoints must follow the terms of this policy and applicable data protection law.

§ 35  Data protection
(1) The Provider will use the personal information the Customer provides to administer this policy and to handle claims.
(2) The Provider will keep personal information only for as long as it is needed for these purposes or as required by law.
(3) The Customer can ask for a copy of the personal information the Provider holds by writing to the Provider's data protection officer.

§ 36  Making a claim
(1) The Customer must notify the Provider of a claim within 30 days of the incident. The Provider will not pay any claim notified after that time.
(2) The Provider may appoint a loss adjuster to investigate any claim.
(3) The Customer must provide proof of ownership or of the cost incurred for every item or service claimed.

§ 37  Complaints
(1) If the Customer has a complaint, the Customer should first contact the Provider's customer relations team, quoting the policy number.
(2) The Provider will acknowledge a complaint within five working days and aim to resolve it within eight weeks.
(3) If the Customer remains dissatisfied, the Customer may be able to refer the complaint to an independent ombudsman service.

§ 38  Instalment agreements
(1) If the Customer pays by instalments, the instalment agreement is a separate contract with the finance provider.
(2) Ending the instalment agreement does not cancel this policy, but unpaid premium remains due.
